_doc: Review policy read by review_gate.py. CI reads this file from the PR's base ref as merged there (git show origin/<base>:...), never from the PR head, so a PR cannot remove itself from the list; if the base ref has no copy it uses the trusted default-branch checkout. second_family_paths: fnmatch globs ("*" also matches "/"); a diff touching any of them needs a passing review (CLEAN, or FINDINGS disposed) from TWO different model families before the review check goes green. The list holds the auth and identity surfaces and the governance-sensitivity manifest's files (_boundary). See docs/operations/github-workflow-conventions.md#second-family-review.
_boundary: Listed: the core gates, files whose main job is an authentication or authorisation decision (OAuth, identity and auth modules and schema, the REST strict-identity gate, dialectic authorization, API keys, effect grants, lease authorization, identity attestation, the MCP authorization gate and its listener config, the BEAM auth plugs and the routers that mount them, the middleware step list), plus the strong-model host adapter and agy client, the dialectic reviewer's backends, its host list and reviewer.py (whose withhold rule decides whether a verdict may release a paused agent; added 2026-10-04 with docs/proposals/active/dialectic-reviewer-hosts-v0.md, as the one large file kept because approval is its job), and the review gate itself. Also listed, whole-file, since 2026-11-20: every file in scripts/dev/governance_sensitivity_manifest.tsv (the enforcement constants and mechanisms, the anti-gaming tests, and the manifest, its checker and its CI workflow). The manifest matches symbols inside some of those files; this list matches the whole file, so it covers a superset of the manifest's diffs. The merge queue lands a governance-sensitive PR only when its diff touches a file on this list and its review check has passed (operator ruling 2026-11-16, docs/dev/GOVERNANCE_SENSITIVITY.md), which is what makes that review a two-family one; tests/test_pr_babysitter_queue.py fails when a manifest path is missing here. Cost of that addition, measured 2026-11-20 over the previous 60 days: 31 of 896 non-merge commits (3%) touched one of those files and no file already listed. Deliberately NOT listed (operator decision 2026-09-27, to keep the cost down): large, often-edited files that hold an access decision among much else: mcp_server.py (auth wiring), mcp_handlers/updates/phases.py (the sync_state write gate), mcp_handlers/decorators.py (which calls need identity), mcp_handlers/stakes_table.py (which need a governance verdict); also files with a single incidental check (http_routes/sentinel.py, mcp_server_std.py, dialectic_protocol.py, mcp_handlers/wave3a_probe.py, mcp_handlers/consolidated.py) and record-integrity signers (dialectic_receipt.py, skill_attestations.py). Adding the four large files back raised coverage from 22% to 27% of code commits. Cost, measured 2026-09-27 over the previous 60 days: 135 of 623 commits touching src/, elixir/ or scripts/dev/ (22%), 9% of all commits. Audited across src/ and elixir/ by grepping for strict-identity refusals, compare_digest, CSRF, WebAuthn, trusted-network checks, signing, attestation, credential minting and verification, and reading each candidate's module docstring. A dispose --emit or hand-rendered record from a TRUSTED author is not verified beyond its shape; the rule guards against honest single-family review, not against a maintainer who could equally post a false CLEAN.
